learningObjective: Separate the bounded implementation work delegated to a coding agent from the contract setting, independent verification, and acceptance authority retained by the engineer.
mediumRationale: Two labelled semantic-HTML lanes make the ownership boundary explicit while preserving a readable ordered sequence in each lane. This is smaller and more accessible than a process diagram, and it reflows into one column without hiding the comparison.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a flowchart would imply one linear handoff and obscure that agent execution and reviewer control overlap throughout the change.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: custom vector geometry adds fixed-width labels and accessibility work without conveying more than two ordered semantic lanes.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: headings and ordered lists expose both ownership and sequence to visual and screen-reader users, while the existing two-panel primitive stacks at narrow widths.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: revealing stages or simulating approve/reject decisions would add state without changing the central ownership distinction.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: neither source provides a suitably scoped workflow figure, and public availability is not treated as artwork-reuse permission.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose enumerates prompting and verification separately, but a side-by-side responsibility boundary makes clear why successful agent execution is evidence rather than acceptance.

pages.insight: The project-setup slide asks the candidate to define goals, evaluation, performance constraints, and project constraints before selecting an implementation.
The production-serving slide calls for a model-gating procedure and explicit experiments or tests before a model is accepted.
The Rules of Machine Learning Engineering slide says to test infrastructure independently from ML, detect silent failures, assign owners, and quantify undesirable behavior.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed for agent, agentic, coding, codebase, review, test, merge, distributed, metric, and confusion-matrix terms. It has no coding-agent or unfamiliar-codebase slide. Pages 165, 168, and 169 are the closest evidence for requirements, gating, independent tests, and human analysis; their full neighborhood, pages 164-170, was inspected. Pages 166-167 cover data pipelines and modeling, while page 170 begins algorithms and data structures, so none adds an agent-review mechanism. No deck layout or artwork is reused.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Review AI-generated code
sources.usage: Used to verify the sequence of automated checks, review against context and intent, scrutiny for changed or skipped tests, and human judgment over generated code.
sources.license: No documentation prose, example prompt, code, or artwork is copied. The workflow labels and two-lane composition are original; the documentation is cited only for factual review practices.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: About GitHub Copilot cloud agent
sources.usage: Used to verify that an agent can research a repository, plan, change code on a branch, execute tests and linters, expose work in commits and logs, and return artifacts for developer iteration and review.
sources.license: No product screenshot, diagram, prose, or code is reused. The visual independently summarizes the division between agent execution and developer acceptance.

sources.title: MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters
sources.usage: Used to cross-check the article's mergeability context: a map operation produces intermediate values and a reduce operation merges values associated with a key across partitioned execution.
sources.license: The publication page does not grant permission to reuse the paper's figures. No figure, wording, data, or layout is copied; the article equation and visual use independently written abstractions.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is the control boundary: an agent may perform most visible execution steps, but passing its requested test does not transfer acceptance authority. The visual is an original semantic-HTML arrangement of general workflow concepts, contains no copied source expression, and uses no external media.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected pages 164-170, then checked official GitHub guidance and the original MapReduce publication. The review selected a static two-lane responsibility model rather than a generic agent flowchart.

implementation.accessibility: The figure uses a labelled heading, a descriptive group label, semantic section headings, and ordered lists. Agent and reviewer ownership is written in every lane and stage rather than encoded by color. The existing two-panel primitive stacks into one column below 640 pixels for a 390 CSS-pixel viewport, uses theme tokens in dark mode, and switches to a high-contrast light palette with page-break protection in print.
